item.title: Bichi assures APC of Tinubu, Yusuf’s victory in 2027
item.description: By Hadiza Yusuf The Chairman of the House of Representatives Committee on Appropriations, Abubakar Kabir Bichi, has expressed confidence that the All Progressives Congress (APC) will secure victory for President Bola Tinubu and Kano State Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf in the 2027 general elections. Bichi made the declaration on Sunday during a strategic meeting with APC members of the Kano State House of Assembly and 40 party candidates at his office in Bichi Local Government Area of the state. The lawmaker, who represents Bichi Federal Constituency, said the meeting was convened to strengthen cooperation among party members and develop strategies for the forthcoming elections. “I brought together APC members of the State House of Assembly and 40 candidates to discuss campaign strategies and coordinate our efforts towards securing victory for President Tinubu, Governor Yusuf and the party in the 2027 general elections,” he said. Bichi thanked the Speaker of the Kano State House of Assembly, Jibril Ismail Falgore, and other participants for attending the meeting. “I appreciate the Speaker and all members for honouring the invitation. Unity is our strength, and together we will deliver victory, Insha Allah,” he said. The post Bichi assures APC of Tinubu, Yusuf’s victory in 2027 appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Millions of Nigerian workers face growing social security risks, NSITF warns
item.description: By Victor Ahiuma-Young The Nigeria Social Insurance Trust Fund, NSITF, has raised the alarm over growing social security risks facing Nigerian workers, warning that the rapid transformation of the labour market through artificial intelligence, AI, automation, digital platforms and the gig economy could leave millions of workers without adequate protection. The Fund has consequently called for urgent measures to close existing social protection gaps, strengthen employer compliance and build a sustainable safety net that guarantees workers’ welfare, dignity and economic security, irrespective of their employment arrangements. The NSITF also emphasised the need for government, employers, organised labour, social security institutions and the media to work together to ensure that technological advancement and changing employment patterns do not create a new generation of economically active but inadequately protected workers. The Managing Director/Chief Executive of NSITF, Oluwaseun Faleye, raised the concerns in his keynote address at the Labour Writers’ Association of Nigeria (LAWAN) Annual Workshop, in Lagos, The address, titled Social Security and Workers’ Welfare in Nigeria’s Political Transition: Closing the Protection Gaps and Building a Sustainable Safety Net, was presented on his behalf by the Deputy General Manager, and Head of Corporate Affairs Department, Alexandra Mede. Faleye described social security as an investment in human dignity, social stability and economic resilience, insisting that its importance should not be measured merely by institutional structures, regulations, financial contributions and statistics. According to him, social security is fundamentally about protecting workers and their families against unforeseen circumstances, including workplace injuries, disabilities, occupational accidents and the sudden loss of a family’s principal breadwinner. He said, “At its heart, social security is about people. It is about the worker who suffers an injury in the course of employment. It is about the family that suddenly loses its principal breadwinner. It is about a worker whose ability to earn an income is affected by an occupational accident.” The NSITF MD/CEO warned that Nigeria’s rapidly changing world of work was creating new challenges for traditional social protection systems, particularly with the growing adoption of technology, artificial intelligence, remote work, automation and digital employment platforms. While acknowledging the opportunities associated with these developments, he expressed concern that workers operating within emerging employment arrangements might be left outside established social protection structures. item.title: Dino Melaye challenges Tinubu to Quranic citation contest
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Former Kogi West Senator and ADC Chieftain, Dino Melaye, has challenged President Bola Tinubu to a Quranic citation contest, following the President’s ongoing spiritual visit to Saudi Arabia for Umrah, the lesser Hajj. Melaye issued the challenge in a post on his X handle on Monday, saying he was ready to compete with Tinubu in citing passages from the Quran when the President returns to Nigeria. He wrote, “Now that Alhaji Bola Tinubu is in Umrah. Immediately he comes back I challenge him to a Quanic citation competition with me. No one can mock God. SDM” Now that Alhaji Bola Tinubu is in Umrah. Immediately he comes back I challenge him to a Quanic citation competition with me. No one can mock God. SDM pic.twitter.com/lssJkwMUz6 — Senator Dino Melaye. (SDM) (@_dinomelaye) November 2, 2026 The challenge comes amid public attention surrounding Tinubu’s spiritual activities in Makkah, where he performed the Umrah pilgrimage and was granted access to pray inside the Holy Ka’abah. Vanguard reported that Tinubu arrived in Saudi Arabia on Thursday, October 29, ahead of the religious exercise, which he performed at the Grand Mosque, Masjid al-Haram, on Friday, October 30. The President was granted the rare privilege of entering the sacred structure by Saudi Arabia’s King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques. According to the Presidency, Sheikh Dahlulah Muthawal of Masjid al-Haram led Tinubu into the Ka’abah, where he offered prayers of gratitude and sought divine guidance for Nigeria. In his reflection on the spiritual experience, Tinubu said he had prayed for wisdom and resilience to continue serving Nigerians. He also cited Surah Aal-Imran, Verse 26 of the Quran, which speaks about Allah’s ultimate authority over power and sovereignty. “There is no other God but Almighty Allah. He is the giver and the taker. He owns power and authority,” the President said. Tinubu subsequently reaffirmed his commitment to national development, saying his determination to build a prosperous Nigeria had been strengthened by the spiritual experience. The President travelled to Saudi Arabia with a delegation that included the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Lateef Fagbemi; Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Professor Muhammad Ali Pate; and governors of Borno, Sokoto, Jigawa, Kaduna, Yobe and Kwara states, among other officials and business leaders. item.title: Mutfwang vows to protect every inch of Plateau land
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa, Jos Plateau State Governor, Caleb Mutfwang, has vowed to protect every inch of the state’s territory, assuring residents that his administration will intensify security efforts and facilitate the return of internally displaced persons (IDPs) to their ancestral communities. Mutfwang gave the assurance on Monday in Jos during the formal inauguration of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Campaign Council, where he also called on party members to intensify grassroots mobilisation ahead of the 2027 general elections. The governor said his administration remained committed to protecting communities and preventing further displacement, adding that efforts were underway to strengthen security operations across the state. “If the people of Plateau knew the magnitude of the damage planned against our state, they would appreciate that only God’s intervention and our strategic efforts have helped us thus far. “One thing I have committed myself to is that I will ensure the protection of every inch of land in Plateau State. “Very soon, we are going to be taking practical steps to facilitate the return of internally displaced persons back to their communities,” he said. Mutfwang disclosed that his administration would deploy additional security personnel, announcing plans to commission a new batch of retrained Operation Rainbow operatives the following week. He added that at least 800 trained forest guards would also be deployed within four weeks as part of efforts to strengthen security across the state. “One of the things we have waited for is to get more boots on ground and, by the grace of God, next week we are going to commission a new batch of retrained Operation Rainbow operatives. “And in another four weeks, we are going to also release at least 800 trained forest guards. “We are determined to ensure that our people return to their ancestral homes,” the governor said. He commended President Bola Tinubu for what he described as his commitment to the welfare of Nigerians and support for efforts to address insecurity. Mutfwang appealed to residents to remain patient and trust his administration, assuring them that it would continue to work towards restoring peace and security. “And so, all we are asking Plateau people is, trust us, be patient with us, and by the grace of God, you will not regret it,” he said. On the 2027 elections, the governor urged members of the campaign council to take the APC’s message to communities across the state, saying his administration needed another mandate to complete ongoing projects and programmes. He said the campaign would seek the people’s endorsement for a second term to sustain the administration’s development agenda. “We are going to the nooks and crannies of Plateau State to solicit their endorsement and approval for a second time in office because the many things we have begun must not be aborted. “We must ensure that we bring things to a very glorious height,” he said. item.title: Gov Eno Approves 13th-Month Pension For Retirees
item.description: Akwa Ibom State Governor, Pastor Umo Eno, has approved the payment of a 13th-month pension bonus to all pensioners in the State, as well as a N10,000 one-time welfare support for November, 2026. Governor Umo Eno disclosed this during the presentation of a Merit Award by the State Council of the Nigeria Union of Pensioners, who also endorsed him for re-election in 2027. Governor Eno, who was particularly impressed by their sense of gratitude and quality organisation, assured that the Government under his leadership will continue to prioritize the welfare of pensioners and elderly citizens in the State. “This is indeed humbling to me. It shows that you are truly technocrats with a laudable sense of organization. You may be retired but not tired. I celebrate and appreciate you greatly. “I am now directing that N10,000 be added to the November 2026 pension payment of every pensioner in support of your welfare,” he said. Governor of Akwa Ibom State, Pastor Umo Eno waves to retirees at the meeting. He urged them to equally enroll in the State’s health insurance scheme, which he said was free for 65-year-olds and above, to enable them to enjoy quality healthcare and a good rest across the state. Gov noted that he had promised to clear the backlog of gratuities, stressing that N100 billion has so far been paid, from the accumulated N111 billion since 2012, assuring that before the end of his first term, the balance will be cleared. He commended President Bola Ahmed Tinubu for making funds available to states, which, according to him, has made it possible for him to keep to his promise of clearing the arrears of gratuity. Governor Umo Eno during the presentation of a Merit Award by the State Council of the Nigeria Union of Pensioners. Earlier, in his welcome remarks, the State Chairman of the Nigeria Union of Pensioners, Pastor Sylvester Nkodo, thanked the Governor for his compassionate and impactful leadership, describing his commitment to the welfare of the elderly and retired public servants as heartwarming and unprecedented. He also noted that Gov. Eno’s policies have significantly improved their living standard and lifted them from abject poverty to a life of dignity. He expressed gratitude to the Governor for the release of over N100 billion for the payment of inherited gratuities dating back to 2012 and prayed that God will grant the wishes of pensioners by granting him a second term in 2027. Following a motion moved and seconded by Comrade James Inim and Dr. Mrs. Uduak Udoaka, respectively, the pensioners unanimously endorsed President Tinubu, Senate President Godswill Akpabio, Governor Umo Eno and other candidates of the APC for re-election in 2027. item.title: [VIDEO] God Has Granted Me Wisdom To Continue To Serve Nigerians – Tinubu
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has said that God has granted him the wisdom to continue to rule Nigerians following his recent visit to the holy mosque in Mecca, Saudi Arabia. President Tinubu, while speaking with journalists, said he felt fulfilled after observing prayers at the holy mosque in Ka’aba. “I feel fulfilled and grateful to Almighty Allah for giving us the opportunity and the health. The day went very well. “The prayer is for Allah to convert our diversity. Nigeria is full of diversity. It is made up of all the faiths. May Allah convert all the diversity to prosperity for the country. That is my prayer”. Speaking on his requests while there, Tinubu noted that God had granted him the “wisdom to continue to serve Nigerians”. “Well, I asked for wisdom and resilience to continue to serve the people. I know that has been granted. “Prior to the 2023 election, I did the same thing. I asked Allah to bless my Umrah then. He did, and I promised that I would come back to thank him, Almighty Allah. “There is no other God but him. He is the giver and the taker. “He owns the power. He said, use it well. If you don’t use it in accordance with my dictates, I can take it from you and give it to another person. “So, I have faith in that and believe extremely well that he has done me a favour to be the president of this great country. On commitment to Nigeria, President Tinubu noted that his commitment is “higher” and determined to bring prosperity. “My commitment is higher, and committed to bringing prosperity. To develop the country consistently with the wish of Allah and the support of the people”. He enjoined all to serve Allah and be guided by their consciences. “It is important to put Allah first. Then follow your conscience, follow the right path that will lead Nigeria to that greatness.” He reiterated that the economy was out of the woods and that the reforms were yielding good results. “The foundation is solid. The economy has come out of the dark tunnel. It is inspiring. We need to build the future for our youths. “If we don’t invest for their future, in 50 years from now, how do we want to be remembered as leaders? I am not looking for anything else.” He thanked management of the Ka’abha for granting him access to the holy mountain, saying that it was a historical moment for him. He assured Nigerians that the current economic challenges would soon be over. “I want to thank everyone for the faith and recognition. I can’t believe that the colour of the Ka’aba was green-white-green. I thank them for the hospitality and recognition given to me as a leader of the delegation. “We are all facing challenges and hostility around us. We will overcome it with faith in the Almighty. “I am grateful forever. I thank the King and the royal crown prince. It is their honour to have allowed me to enter the Ka’aba. It is history.” The post [VIDEO] God Has Granted Me Wisdom To Continue To Serve Nigerians – Tinubu appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Tinubu inherited Nigeria on brink of collapse from Buhari — Plateau gov
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa, Jos Plateau State Governor, Caleb Mutfwang, has said President Bola Ahmed Tinubu inherited a Nigerian economy that was “tottering on the brink of collapse” from the administration of former President Muhammadu Buhari in 2023. Mutfwang stated this on Monday during the formal inauguration of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Campaign Council in Jos, where he also defended the Tinubu administration’s economic reforms and urged Plateau residents to support the President in the 2027 election. “Where did President Tinubu meet Nigeria in 2023? He met Nigeria, tottering on the brink of collapse, Nigeria that could not service its external debts, Nigeria that would not even allow businesses outside the country to take their proceeds back home.” “And that is why some international airlines stopped flying to Nigeria, because they could not get the dollars to take back their money.” “Our external reserve was down to just a little over $3 billion, from the over $40 billion it had accumulated for decades.” “Today, by the grace of God, we have a healthy external reserve of over $50 billion,” he said. Mutfwang further alleged that the previous administration resorted to printing money to manage the economy, claiming that more than N30 trillion was printed. “When the President took over in 2023, the government that he succeeded had run out of ideas on how to manage the economy, and they resorted to printing money in the Central Bank. “They printed over N30 trillion, which went down the drain.” “Today, by the grace of God, the Central Bank has stabilised, and that deficit has been done away with,” the governor said. On fuel subsidy, Mutfwang described the system under the previous administration as fraudulent, alleging that the country borrowed money to pay claims supported by what he called fictitious documents. “I say it was a fraud because we were borrowing money to pay people who brought fictitious documents. They never brought any wealth. They brought fictitious documents, claimed monies and subsidies. “You cannot continue to borrow money to give to thieves. You have to stop it at some point. And when it is stopped, there will be a payback; there will be a recovery time,” he said. The governor said the availability of fuel had improved despite the increase in its cost, recalling the long queues that previously characterised fuel stations across the country. “Today, by the grace of God, we have solved one side of the equation. Today fuel is available. It may not be cheap, but it is available.” “Those of us who are in my age bracket or a little below will remember the times when we spent days in petrol stations queuing for fuel that we could hardly get. But we have been able to resolve that,” Mutfwang said. item.title: Oyedepo ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‌‍⁠​‌⁠​‍‌​tasks Africa with indigenous solutions to challenges
item.description: The Chancellor of Covenant University, Ota, Ogun, Dr David Oyedepo, has urged African countries to look inward and deploy indigenous solutions to address the continent’s numerous challenges. Oyedepo gave the advice in an interview with the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) on Monday in Ota. He said that developing homegrown solutions to local challenges was the way forward for Africa to reduce its heavy dependence on foreign countries. “Man is created to solve his problems wherever he is planted. Therefore, African countries should provide solutions to their challenges without constantly seeking foreign assistance,” he said. The chancellor said that Africa’s slow pace of development was not because its people were Black but largely because they were blind to their potential. ‘’Africans should take absolute responsibility for their destiny,” he said. Oyedepo attributed the continent’s inability to adequately address its challenges to what he described as a “what will happen will happen” mentality. According to him, the mindset has contributed significantly to Africa’s present situation by discouraging proactive thinking and responsibility. He said that the greatness of any nation depended on the valuable contributions of individuals and organisations within its borders. ‘’Africa will make meaningful progress only when its countries recognise the importance of indigenous solutions and take responsibility for addressing their challenges rather than relying excessively on foreign assistance,” he said. The chancellor urged African leaders and citizens to harness their local knowledge, resources and capabilities to drive sustainable development across the continent. item.title: Bauchi LGA chairman dies in auto crash after APM meeting
item.description: By Christopher Ameh, Bauchi The Chairman of Zaki Local Government Area of Bauchi State, Masud Aliyu Umar, has died in a road accident while returning from an Allied Peoples Movement (APM) stakeholders’ meeting in Bauchi. Umar reportedly died on Sunday night when his private car crashed at Konkiyal Village in Darazo Local Government Area, about 100 kilometres from Bauchi metropolis. The late chairman was returning to Zaki after attending the political meeting when the accident occurred. Before his election as Zaki LGA chairman on August 17, 2026, Umar served as Director-General of the Bauchi State Emergency Management Agency, SEMA. Reacting to his death, Governor Bala Mohammed expressed shock, describing the deceased as a dedicated public servant, committed grassroots politician and compassionate leader whose contributions to public service and community development would remain indelible in the history of the state. In a condolence message issued by his media aide, Mukhtar Gidado, the governor said Umar’s tenure at SEMA was marked by his commitment to alleviating the suffering of vulnerable citizens and providing timely interventions to communities affected by emergencies and humanitarian challenges. Mohammed added that as chairman of Zaki Local Government, the deceased demonstrated commitment to grassroots development through initiatives aimed at empowering youths and women, improving livelihoods and promoting inclusive development. He described the death as a devastating loss to the deceased’s family, the people of Zaki and Bauchi State, particularly the public service and local government administration. The governor urged the family, political associates, friends and people of Zaki Local Government to find strength and comfort in Almighty Allah during the difficult period. The funeral prayer is scheduled for Monday, November 2, 2026, at 2pm at the Palace of the District Head, Mur Mur, Zaki Local Government Area of Bauchi State. item.title: [Updated] Iran says ready to reopen Hormuz in two days if US agrees to demands
item.description: Iran on Monday said it was ready to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days if the US agrees to its conditions, having previously proposed a one-week timeline. “The possibility of implementing this plan in two days is another indication of Iran’s good-faith approach,” said foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei. “We have stated that, if Iran’s demands are met, it would be possible to restore security to the Strait of Hormuz and resume the negotiating process within a short period.” He said an exchange of messages was ongoing with the United States via mediators and that “everything depends” on the US side accepting the Iranian demands. “Only then can we discuss the subsequent stages.” Since the Middle East war broke out in late February, Iran has claimed control over Hormuz, a vital energy conduit for shipping. It regularly targets vessels that attempt to cross the strait without its authorisation, while the US has in retaliation imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports. In September, Iran initially proposed a seven-day plan that it conveyed to the US through Qatar, which would have seen Tehran reopen Hormuz on the sixth day after the US met Iranian demands. Those demands include ending the Middle East war on all fronts, the unfreezing of Iranian assets abroad, lifting sanctions on its oil sector, and an end to the US naval blockade. In an interview with Al Jazeera released on Sunday, Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Washington must accept a new route agreed between Iran and Oman for transit through the strait. He said the US must also remove sanctions imposed in recent months and reduce American troop numbers in the region. Washington has since August rolled out a fresh raft of sanctions, part of what it called “economic asphyxiation” of Iran. The United States and Israel have in recent days also intensified threats to renew attacks on Iran amid crucial elections in both countries. On Saturday, US President Donald Trump said he still had to “take care” of one or two targets including Pickaxe mountain in central Iran, a suspected nuclear site which Tehran denies is such a facility. “Any act of aggression against Iran, any military attack against Iran, by whatever means, will be met with a powerful, immediate and comprehensive response from us,” said Baqaei during a foreign ministry briefing Monday. item.title: Entering Holy Kaaba with Tinubu a blessing beyond measure – Abdul Samad Rabiu
item.description: Billionaire industrialist and Chairman of BUA Group, Abdul Samad Rabiu, has described his entry into the Holy Kaaba alongside President Bola Tinubu as a rare spiritual privilege and an experience he would cherish for the rest of his life. Rabiu disclosed this in a Facebook post on Sunday night, sharing a photograph of himself with Tinubu He wrote, “Some moments in life are beyond words, moments that touch the soul and remain forever engraved in the heart. “Alhamdulillah, today I was profoundly humbled and blessed to be among those granted the extraordinary honour of entering the Holy Kaaba alongside His Excellency, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR. “It was a once-in-a-lifetime blessing, an honour beyond measure, and a moment of divine grace that will remain etched in my heart for as long as I live.” Rabiu said his prayers at the sacred site extended beyond himself and his family to Nigeria, expressing hope for lasting peace, unity and prosperity in the country. He added, “In that most sacred of places, my thoughts and prayers were not only for myself and my family, but for our entire nation. “May Almighty Allah accept our prayers and bless our beloved nation with lasting peace, unity, and prosperity.” Rabiu was among the delegation that accompanied Tinubu to Makkah for Umrah, the lesser pilgrimage, on Friday, which included Oando Group Chief Executive Officer, Wale Tinubu, state governors and other senior government officials. Speaking at a dinner hosted for members of the delegation in Makkah on Saturday, Rabiu pledged the continued support of the business community for the administration and thanked the president for the rare spiritual opportunity. Tinubu had also told journalists after performing the Umrah that he felt fulfilled, describing the experience as spiritual. item.title: African players in Europe: Defender Hakimi’s historic hat-trick
item.description: Reigning African Footballer of the Year and Paris Saint-Germain defender Achraf Hakimi claimed a first career hat-trick at the weekend in a 5-1 Ligue 1 rout of bottom club Le Havre. Meanwhile, Nicolas Jackson continued to defy critics from a difficult spell at Chelsea by scoring his eighth goal in 12 appearances for Aston Villa, who drew 1-1 with Fulham. AFP Sport highlights African headline-makers in the major European leagues: FRANCE ACHRAF HAKIMI (Paris Saint-Germain) Morocco captain Hakimi was involved in all five goals as defending European champions and Ligue 1 leaders PSG inflicted a seventh defeat in nine matches on Le Havre. Apart from his hat-trick, he set up goals for Mika Godts and Senny Mayulu. ENGLAND NICOLAS JACKSON (Aston Villa) In-form Jackson scored again, but it was not enough for Unai Emery’s men to defeat struggling Fulham. The Senegal international coolly slotted home from Johan Manzambi’s pass for a fifth Premier League goal in his last five games. TAIWO AWONIYI (Coventry City) Awoniyi netted his first league goal for Coventry in a 3-1 win over Sunderland that hauled the Sky Blues out of the relegation zone. The Nigerian made the most of his first start since September as he won possession himself before surging into the Sunderland box and firing into the bottom corner. SPAIN YAN DIOMANDE (Real Madrid) Ivory Coast teenager Diomande completed the scoring before half-time as Real Madrid triumphed 3-0 at Racing Santander in La Liga. The record signing by the 15-time European champions lashed home from the edge of the box after 37 minutes. ITALY M’BALA NZOLA (Cagliari) Angolan Nzola gave mid-table Cagliari the lead midway through the first half, but Serie A pacesetters Lazio hit back to win 2-1 in Rome. Nzola struck from the edge of the six-yard box to net in successive matches for the first time in 70 months. GERMANY SERHOU GUIRASSY (Borussia Dortmund) His second-half goal put Borussia on track for an impressive 2-2 Bundesliga draw at leaders Bayern Munich. After Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane missed a penalty, Dortmund went to the other end of the pitch and Guirassy equalised. It brought the goal tally of the Guinea striker in all competitions to eight this season. IBRAHIM MAZA (Bayer Leverkusen) Leverkusen were outplayed by Stuttgart in a 4-2 defeat, but Maza left the pitch with his head held high. After the Algeria midfielder showcased his stunning dribbling, he scored after 79 minutes with an unstoppable header. BILAL EL KHANNOUSS (Stuttgart) El Khannouss provided the creative spark as Stuttgart snapped a run of poor form to win at Leverkusen. The Moroccan scored with a superb low shot early in the second half and helped create Stuttgart’s fourth for Ermedin Demirovic. item.title: Tinubu reaffirms commitment to Project Nigeria
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has reaffirmed his commitment to Project Nigeria, pledging to build a prosperous nation, invest in youths and pursue development guided by Almighty Allah and Nigerians’ aspirations. The president stated this on Monday while reflecting on his spiritual journey to Saudi Arabia for the lesser Hajj, during which he was granted the rare privilege of praying inside the Holy Ka’abah. King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques, granted the President and members of his delegation access to the sacred structure in Makkah. At the Ka’abah, Tinubu offered prayers of gratitude to Almighty Allah for the privilege of serving as Nigeria’s president and commander-in-chief of the armed forces. Sheikh Dahlulah Muthawal of Masjid al-Haram led the President into the Ka’abah. Tinubu thanked King Salman and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman for granting him and members of his delegation the opportunity to enter the Holy Ka’abah and offer prayers. He described the honour as historic and a deeply cherished spiritual experience, reflecting the longstanding bonds of friendship, mutual respect and cooperation between Nigeria and Saudi Arabia. “I want to say a big thank you for the faith, for the recognition. I can’t believe the fencing of the Ka’abah is in green-white-green, which reminds us of the Nigerian identity. “I thank the Crown Prince and all the administrators of the Holy Land. I thank them for the hospitality and recognition given to me as the leader of the delegation and the country. “We are all facing challenges and hostility around us. We will overcome them with faith in God Almighty. I’m grateful forever. I thank the King and the royal Crown Prince. “It is an honour that I enjoyed, and it is gracious of them to have allowed me to enter inside the Ka’abah. This is history,” he said. The president said he prayed for wisdom and resilience to continue serving Nigerians, expressing confidence that Almighty Allah had granted his request. “Well, I asked for wisdom and resilience to continue to serve the people. I know that prayer has been granted. Before the 2023 election, I did the same thing. “I asked Allah to bless my Umrah then, and He did. And I promised that I would come back to thank Him,” the President said. Reflecting on Surah Aal-Imran, Verse 26 of the Holy Qur’an, the President said sovereignty belonged ultimately to Almighty Allah, who grants and withdraws power. He said the message underscored the need for leaders to exercise authority responsibly, with humility and in the service of the people. “There is no other God but Almighty Allah. item.title: Sultan Turbans two sons, Murtala Dan’Iyan as Dallatun Sokoto
item.description: By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto SOKOTO — The Sultan of Sokoto, Alhaji Muhammad Sa’ad Abubakar III, has conferred traditional titles on two of his sons, Alhaji Murtala Abdulkadir Dan’Iyan Jarman Sokoto and 10 other distinguished Nigerians in recognition of their contributions to humanity and community development. The ceremony, held on Sunday at the Sultan’s Palace in Sokoto, also witnessed the turbaning of two biological sons of the Sultan. Alhaji Abubakar Sadiq was turbaned Sarkin Dawakin Tsakar Gida, while Alhaji Shehu Abubakar received the title of Fagacin Sokoto. The event marked the climax of a three-day programme organised by friends, associates and well-wishers of the new Dallatun Sokoto to celebrate his elevation into the traditional institution of the Sokoto Caliphate. It attracted traditional rulers, politicians, senior government officials, Islamic scholars, business executives and community leaders from within and outside Nigeria. Among those honoured were Alhaji Abubakar Hussain, who received the title of Sarkin Bai; Alhaji Aminu Isa-Buhari, Danmalikin Sokoto; Professor Mansur Ibrahim, Danmasanin Sokoto; and Professor Ishaq Oloyede, Kuliyan Sokoto. Others were Dr Peter Igoh, Kakakin Daular Usmaniya; Representative Almustapha Rabah, Bauran Sokoto; Dr Balarabe Kakale, Wakilin Makarantar Daular Usmaniya; Alhaji Bello Abbas, Wakilin Tarihin Daular Usmaniya; and Alhaji Gandi Umar, Sarkin Galmar Sarkin Musulmi. Speaking at the ceremony, the Sultan described the turbaning as a historic occasion organised by the Sultanate Council to recognise individuals whose contributions and achievements in their respective fields had distinguished them as worthy ambassadors of the Caliphate. He said the traditional institution would continue to recognise and honour sons and daughters of the Caliphate who demonstrated commitment, integrity and outstanding performance in their various endeavours. The monarch, however, reminded the new title holders that their elevation should not be regarded merely as a ceremonial honour but as a call to greater service and responsibility to their communities and society. He urged them to remain their brothers’ keepers, promote peace, unity and peaceful coexistence, and offer constructive ideas to strengthen harmonious relationships within the Caliphate, Sokoto State and Nigeria. In separate interviews after the ceremony, prominent personalities described the new Dallatun Sokoto as humble, honest and trustworthy, citing his philanthropic activities and readiness to assist people across religious, ethnic and social divides. A father figure and mentor to the new title holder, Alhaji Umarun Kwabo AA Jarman Sokoto, described him as loyal, humble and dependable, saying his commitment to the service of God and humanity had earned him the confidence of those around him. “I am optimistic that Dallatun Sokoto, Alhaji Murtala Abdulkadir Dan’Iyan Jarman Sokoto, will wear the shoes and crown in the service of God and humanity,” Kwabo said.

item.title: Iran Warns New War Could Last Longer After Trump Threatens Strikes
item.description: Iran warned on Sunday that any renewed war with the United States could last longer than the previous round of fighting, after President Donald Trump said he still had to “take care” of more targets. Diplomatic efforts to end the Middle East war have been punctuated by repeated threats from the United States and Israel to resume bombardments as they hold crucial elections. “A potential future war could last longer than previous conflict, and the American president would not be in a position to dictate the timing or the conditions of its conclusion,” said army spokesman Mohammad Akraminia, according to Iranian state television. In the most intense phase of the war, which began on February 28 with US-Israeli strikes on Iran, Tehran retaliated with missile and drone attacks across the region. Iran-aligned armed groups joined the fighting in Lebanon and Yemen. Akraminia’s remarks followed Trump’s suggestion that the United States could swiftly strike its remaining targets in Iran. “We still have to take care of, I would say one or two sites, but we can do that in 10 minutes,” Trump told reporters. “You probably could look at Pickaxe Mountain, and you have to take care of that. We can do that all very quickly,” he added, referring to a suspected underground nuclear complex. Trump reiterated his threat on Sunday, telling a campaign rally in Iowa ahead of midterm elections, that he may have to give Tehran “the hammer” at some unspecified time. The warning came after US media reported that Trump had held a call with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Saturday over whether and when to ramp up combat operations against the Islamic republic. Axios quoted one US and one Israeli official saying the two leaders discussed the state of negotiations with Iran, with Netanyahu pressing the president to strike the country immediately after Tuesday’s US midterm elections and Trump eager to let negotiations play out. The Israeli source described the call as “tough”, while the US source said it was “direct”, according to Axios. Speaking to reporters on Sunday, Trump confirmed he had discussed Iran with Netanyahu, but would not elaborate. A woman walks past a mural bearing the Iranian national flag in Tehran on October 26, 2026. ‘No Geographical Limitations’ Top military and political officials in Iran have warned against any new attack. Revolutionary Guards spokesman Hossein Mohebbi on Sunday echoed a warning issued a day earlier in a written message by Iran’s new supreme leader, Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei. “In a conflict with America, there are no geographical limitations; a vast theatre has been defined for inflicting damage upon the enemy,” Mohebbi said, according to state television. Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said: “We hope the other side will exercise rationality and choose diplomacy,” adding that Iran “remains prepared for both defence and diplomacy”, according to the official IRNA news agency. item.title: Fresh woes for pupils in Niger
item.description: At least 12 pupils of Madarasatul Nurul Islam, Maikujeri community in Rafi Local Government Area of Niger State have been reportedly kidnapped by bandits. Daily Trust gathered that the children were abducted around 10am on Saturday while harvesting maize on their teacher’s farm on the outskirts of the town. A resident, Mohammed Adamu, told Daily Trust that the children were already on their way home when the bandits struck and picked them. An Okada man identified as Tasi’u, who attempted to escape, was reportedly shot and is currently receiving treatment at the IBB Specialist Hospital in Minna, the state capital. How bureaucracy leaves power equipment rotting in ports Sokoto: Concerns over attack on ADC guber candidate’s convoy Another source close to the Quranic school told one of our correspondents that 13 people, including 12 female pupils of the school and the younger brother of the school’s proprietor, Mallam Mainasara, were kidnapped. He said the victims, aged between nine and 14, were abducted as they stopped by a borehole to wash themselves and drink water after leaving the farm. According to him, the pupils had been working on the farm with their teacher when the teacher received information that bandits were advancing towards the area. He said the teacher immediately instructed the pupils to return home while he also left on his motorcycle. “While on their way home, the pupils reportedly stopped at a borehole to wash their bodies and drink water. It was at that point that the armed men swooped on them and whisked them away,” he said. The source further disclosed that some women were also abducted from another farm in the area. When contacted, the spokesperson for the Niger Police Command, SP Wasiu Abiodun, promised to verify the information and revert. The police spokesperson, however, revealed that six people were rescued but was silent on the abduction of the pupils. He said, “On 29th October, 2026, at about 12.30pm, joint security tactical teams during a clearance and rescue operation around Pandogari Rafi LGA rescued six abducted victims who were reportedly kidnapped by some hoodlums on 28th October, 2026 at about 12 pm in their farms at Mahangi village via Pandogari. “The victims were abducted and taken to Hanawanka forest where they were rescued unhurt. They were later received at Kagara Div for debriefing and medical attention ahead of reunion with their relatives.” Map of Niger State with red cycle indicating the LGA where the incident took place Dozens of farmers displaced Similarly, dozens of farming communities in Borgu, Mariga, Mashegu and Rijau LGAs have continued to flee their homes following the renewed bandits’ attacks. The affected farmers told Daily Trust that their farm produce, including rice, soyabeans and maize, is wasting on their farms because bandits have stopped them from harvesting.
